{"themes":[{"machine_theme_id":"M1","label":"Gender does not influence food choices","one_sentence_description":"Participants agree that gender plays no role in determining what types of food they choose to eat.","relevance":"central","evidence":[{"turn_id":"T002","speaker":"Participant 1","quote":"I don't think so, I don't really understanding how it would. I don't think it would make, makes any difference whatsoever."},{"turn_id":"T003","speaker":"Participant 2","quote":"But in terms of, of what I eat, um no, no, not in terms of a choice of what I eat."},{"turn_id":"T004","speaker":"Participant 3","quote":"I don't really think that it influences what I might eat."}],"voiced_by":["Participant 1","Participant 2","Participant 3"]},{"machine_theme_id":"M2","label":"Shared family meals dictate diet over individual gender preferences","one_sentence_description":"Eating together as a family means sharing the same meals, which prevents gender from creating differences in what individuals eat.","relevance":"secondary","evidence":[{"turn_id":"T004","speaker":"Participant 3","quote":"so I think, also, I think with this question is I tend to eat with the family. So we all eat together, really. So it's not like I would have a separate portion."}],"voiced_by":["Participant 3"]},{"machine_theme_id":"M3","label":"Health, fitness, and weight control are the primary drivers of food choices","one_sentence_description":"Dietary choices are influenced by active health goals, exercise regimes, and physical training rather than gender.","relevance":"central","evidence":[{"turn_id":"T004","speaker":"Participant 3","quote":"I think if I went out with, I think it's more a question of what's, um, so if people are on a bit of a health push, I mean, that could be guys or, or if you're trying to control your weight, or you're in a bit of a, I think that's more of an influence. It's kind of how you're feeling about what you want to put in your body and how much you're exercising, that sort of thing. I feel that more influences it."},{"turn_id":"T005","speaker":"Participant 2","quote":"So I've got, I've got a mate of mine who's in training at the moment to do a sponsored marathon, that sort of thing. So obviously, he's watching what he eats, but that's not gender based. That's for a specific target, a specific goal."}],"voiced_by":["Participant 2","Participant 3"]},{"machine_theme_id":"M4","label":"Dietary choices like vegetarianism stem from personal belief systems, not gender","one_sentence_description":"Specialized diets such as vegetarianism are driven by an individual's personal ethics or beliefs rather than their gender.","relevance":"secondary","evidence":[{"turn_id":"T005","speaker":"Participant 2","quote":"But again, it's, I don't, I don't believe it's anything to do with their gender, that's more their belief system, therefore wanting to not eat meat."}],"voiced_by":["Participant 2"]},{"machine_theme_id":"M5","label":"Gender may relate to body image and portion sizes rather than food selection","one_sentence_description":"While gender does not influence what specific food is chosen, it can affect concerns regarding body image and portion control.","relevance":"secondary","evidence":[{"turn_id":"T003","speaker":"Participant 2","quote":"I can, maybe genders may come into it, as I say when it comes to, to kind of body image and portions and stuff."}],"voiced_by":["Participant 2"]}]
}

{"themes":[{"machine_theme_id":"M1","label":"Social expectations of masculinity dictate what men are supposed to eat","one_sentence_description":"Men face implicit social expectations and pressure to eat heavy, traditional foods like meat and potatoes, while avoiding lighter options like salad to maintain their masculine identity.","relevance":"central","evidence":[{"turn_id":"T002","speaker":"Participant 1","quote":"You don't eat salad if you're a bloke round here. You just don't. That's what I meant earlier — you stick to what's expected. Meat, potatoes, that sort of thing. That's what men eat."},{"turn_id":"T003","speaker":"Participant 2","quote":"I probably wouldn't order salad down the pub with the lads, not because anyone's said anything, but... you just wouldn't, would you. You'd get a pie or fish and chips or whatever. That feels normal."},{"turn_id":"T009","speaker":"Participant 3","quote":"A bloke like me — I work in construction, right. I'm 53, I've got mates, I go to the pub. I'm not fashionable or... I dunno, concerned with that sort of thing. I'm straightforward. I eat proper food, meat and that. I don't fuss about what I'm eating or where it comes from or whether it's healthy or whatever."}],"voiced_by":["Participant 1","Participant 2","Participant 3"]},{"machine_theme_id":"M2","label":"Inability to distinguish personal preference from internalized social pressure","one_sentence_description":"Social expectations and gender norms are internalized so deeply over time that individuals can no longer differentiate between their genuine personal preferences and the pressure to conform.","relevance":"central","evidence":[{"turn_id":"T004","speaker":"Participant 1","quote":"It just feels natural because it's what everyone around you does, what you've always done. But that doesn't mean it's what you actually want — it just means you can't tell the difference anymore."},{"turn_id":"T003","speaker":"Participant 2","quote":"I'm not sure if that's because I'm being pressured into it or because that's just what I actually want. Might be the same thing by now, might not be."},{"turn_id":"T007","speaker":"Participant 3","quote":"I'm realizing that's not the same as being free, is it. Because what Mark's saying about not even knowing the difference anymore between what you want and what you've been told to want — I think I've got that too, just dressed up different."}],"voiced_by":["Participant 1","Participant 2","Participant 3"]},{"machine_theme_id":"M3","label":"Conformity is maintained through anticipatory discomfort and the fear of judgment","one_sentence_description":"Men adhere to food expectations because deviating from them triggers an uncomfortable feeling of being noticed, judged, or doing something wrong, even when no explicit rules exist.","relevance":"central","evidence":[{"turn_id":"T002","speaker":"Participant 1","quote":"If you started ordering something different, something lighter or more... I dunno, more careful about it, people would notice. They'd comment. And you'd feel like you're doing something wrong, which is daft when you think about it, but that's how it works."},{"turn_id":"T005","speaker":"Participant 2","quote":"If I walked in and ordered a salad, I'd... I'd feel something. I know I would. Can't really pretend I wouldn't."}],"voiced_by":["Participant 1","Participant 2"]},{"machine_theme_id":"M4","label":"Urban anonymity does not equate to freedom from internalized dietary expectations","one_sentence_description":"While living in a city eliminates the fear of immediate social judgment or comment regarding dietary choices, individuals still experience internalized pressure to conform to traditional masculine roles.","relevance":"secondary","evidence":[{"turn_id":"T007","speaker":"Participant 3","quote":"No one's going to comment if I order a salad — literally no one cares what I eat. But listening to you two, I'm realizing that's not the same as being free, is it."},{"turn_id":"T007","speaker":"Participant 3","quote":"There's no village watching, no mates who'd comment. So I can't even blame it on anything external like you can, Mark. I've just absorbed it somehow."}],"voiced_by":["Participant 3"]}] }
